body.x: Dr. K Health Care (CEO Hyung-jin Kang) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Dr.K Health Care is a company that develops a mobile app for analyzing skin conditions using a special lens attachable to smartphones. The app utilizes a special lens and AI system that can be operated easily and accurately without additional equipment, regardless of the smartphone model. The service emphasizes its convenience and accuracy, making it accessible anywhere with smartphone and internet connectivity.

At this year's CES, Dr.K Health Care highlighted its personalized skin health management program, 'The Skin Fit Program.' The home spa service, Skin Fit Program, optimizes user needs by allowing them to measure their skin condition at home without needing to visit a spa or consult a dermatologist. When customers apply for the service, Dr.K Health Care provides them with the Skin Fit special lens. Users can attach the lens to their smartphones, take close-up photos of different areas of their skin, and submit them through the mobile platform for analysis and tailored solutions.

To enter the global market, Dr.K Health Care is actively advancing technological improvements, considering the diversity of local customers. The company is enhancing its AI model's research and development and expanding the volume of data learning to diagnose skin characteristics based on race more accurately, aiming to improve the suitability of product recommendations. Additionally, Dr.K Health Care participated in CES 2024 to explore partnerships for service provision and maintenance in the global market. The company seeks collaborative partners who can contribute to product packaging, possess a rich understanding of the related industry, and excel in networking capabilities as it ventures into market expansion.

Dr.K Health Care stated, "Skin Fit Platform leverages the network environment and smartphones, allowing users to observe and manage their skin anytime, anywhere, making it our greatest asset." Continued with, "We have already entered major Asian markets such as Japan, Singapore, and Vietnam and will continue to provide services to various markets in the future. Based on expertise in customization, we have enhanced service quality through algorithm localization, considering regional climate, environment, and lifestyle factors."

Furthermore, they mentioned, "During this exhibition, we have received collaboration proposals from domestic companies and international companies such as L'Oréal. It has been a great opportunity for networking and exchange. There was also significant interest from the Latin American region, and other positive outcomes, such as sample orders and sales, were achieved through consultations. While personalized skin care services based on individual skin analysis through smart devices are already prevalent in Korea, this technology remains unknown in the global market. Therefore, we believe that there is tremendous potential in the market."

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
